name: md5(cap(md5($plain)).":".$username)
denotation: MD5CAPMD5USER is MULTI-EMIT: it matches either md5(cap(md5($p)).$u) or md5(cap(md5($p)).":".$u)
notes: This row is mdxfind type MD5CAPMD5USER. CORRECTED TWICE on 2026-08-31, and the second correction matters more than the first. Waffle named the unknown vector d4f7dec5...:abc123 as the colon form, confirmed here by independent Digest::MD5 and by local mdxfind pinned to ^MD5CAPMD5USER$ with -F. But the hx specification (rev 1.15) Appendix A Note [24] then showed the stronger fact: MD5CAPMD5USER is a MULTI-EMIT type. It emits BOTH md5(cap(md5($p)).$u) and md5(cap(md5($p)).":".$u) and matches if either reproduces the stored digest. So this row is not one computation, and neither of its two vectors is anomalous -- 05b56c69... is the colonless emit and d4f7dec5... is the colon emit. The first correction here wrongly called the colonless vector foreign and removed it; it is restored. A copy also sits on md5-md5-pass-salt, which is the row for the colonless construction in its own right. john has no format for either emit: discover-john.pl ran all 957 formats against the colon vector with zero matches, and the dynamic language has no literal-string token. The 198,534-construction sweep that failed to identify this missed it because it enumerated terms and never a literal separator.

name: MD5-SALTMD5PASS-SALT
notes: Split out on 2026-08-30. mdxfind type e818 and hashcat mode 33100 had no entry of their own, and e818's example vector had been seeded onto md5-salt-md5-pass-salt, whose name, id and other vector are the neighbouring construction md5($s.md5($p.$s)) (e515, hashcat 4110). Digest::MD5 - independent of all three crackers - identifies this vector as md5($s.md5($p).$s); hashcat -m 33100, mdxfind pinned to the type, and john dynamic_14 and dynamic_2014 all reproduce it.

name: MD5UCBASE64SHA1RAW
notes: The vendored catalog renders this type's example digest in uppercase hex, and mdxfind will not read it back in that case, so the seeding pass could not verify it. mdxfind -z computes the same digest in lowercase for the same plaintext, and pinned to ^MD5UCBASE64SHA1RAW$ it reproduces that form; the stored vector is the catalog's own digest re-cased, not one we invented. Fourteen other types carry an uppercase example (MD5UC, SHA1UC, SHA256UC, RACF, ORACLE7 among them) and are NOT all the same story -- MD5UC and SHA256UC do not reproduce in either case.
